title: Send crews to flood sites

blocks.text: A river authority sends pump crews to flood sites. Each site needs exactly one crew; each crew goes to at most one site; some crews are not equipped for some sites. The cost of sending a crew to a site is a whole number of $k, given only for the allowed pairs.

Write `assign(crews, sites, cost)` in `sites.py` with `SimpleLinearSumAssignment`. `cost` maps `(crew, site)` to the cost, for allowed pairs only. There are never fewer crews than sites. Return `(total cost, {crew: site})`, listing only the crews that got a site, or `None` when no assignment covers every site.
The model, with $`E`$ the allowed pairs:

`SimpleLinearSumAssignment` gives *every* left node a right node, so the crew rows' "at most one" needs the trick of the lesson's second section. The tests compare your answer with a brute-force search. About twelve lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.graph.python import linear_sum_assignment


def assign(crews: list[str], sites: list[str], cost: dict):
    """Each site gets one crew, each crew at most one site, at least total cost.

    cost: {(crew, site): whole-number cost} over the allowed pairs only. Returns
    (total, {crew: site}) for the crews that got a site, or None if no such assignment exists.
    """
    # TODO: build a SimpleLinearSumAssignment, square it if needed, solve, and read the plan.
    return 0, {}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(assign(["A", "B"], ["north", "south"], {("A", "north"): 3, ("A", "south"): 5, ("B", "north"): 4, ("B", "south"): 9}))

cases.says: with one crew per site and every pair allowed, the assignment is the cheapest one
a crew is never sent to a site it may not take
with more crews than sites, the spare crews get no site and the cost is still the least
when some site has no crew allowed to take it, there is no plan
